meta.name: The World, 1936
meta.description: The whole world on 1 January 1936, from the Arctic to Cape Horn: the British and French empires at their greatest extent with the League mandates, a rearming Germany, the Soviet Union from the Dniester to the Pacific, Italy at war in Ethiopia, Japan with its creature Manchukuo, Nationalist China, and the United States in the Depression. The treaties of the day are in force and the claims of the time stand, Ethiopia and Manchuria among them. Borders approximated from present-day divisions; protectorates are drawn as their protector’s land.
meta.blurb: A huge historical campaign: about 1,600 provinces and 69 realms on the eve of the Second World War.
meta.style: Empires and revisionists across every ocean
attribution: Coastlines, lakes, rivers, first-level divisions and towns: Natural Earth (naturalearthdata.com), public domain.

Borders of 1936 approximated from present-day divisions; historical names, town populations of about 1936, ridges, passes and straits are authored (tools/earth1936.data.ts, with tools/earth.data.ts and tools/europe1936.data.ts). Arms are simplified, in national colours.

regions.name: Great Hungarian Plain and Northern Hungary

nations.name: United Kingdom
nations.summary: The largest empire on earth: the British Isles, India and Burma, half of Africa, the mandates of Palestine, Transjordan and Tanganyika, Malaya and the Caribbean, rearming slowly after the Abyssinian crisis.
nations.strength: Sea power and commerce: trade pays more and fleets are cheap to keep.
nations.constraint: A small army for the largest empire, spread over every continent.

nations.name: Irish Free State
nations.summary: A dominion since 1922, now under de Valera unpicking the Treaty, and in a tariff war with Britain.
nations.strength: Men who fought for independence in living memory: soldiers fight well.
nations.constraint: Small, agricultural and at odds with its largest market.

nations.name: French Republic
nations.summary: The Third Republic behind the Maginot Line, with the second colonial empire: North and West Africa, Madagascar, Indochina and the mandates of Syria, Lebanon, Cameroun and Togo.
nations.strength: Fortifications and a large reserve: forts cost less.
nations.constraint: A falling birth rate and short-lived governments: men are precious.

nations.name: German Reich
nations.summary: Rearming openly since 1935 and rejoined by the Saar, with the Rhineland still demilitarised and the treaties of 1919 its declared grievance.
nations.strength: Industry and staff work: research and income above every neighbour.
nations.constraint: Ringed by French alliances, and short of oil, rubber and iron ore.

nations.name: Kingdom of Italy
nations.summary: Mussolini’s kingdom, at war in Ethiopia and under League sanctions, with Libya, Eritrea, Somaliland and the Dodecanese.
nations.strength: A long coast and a modern fleet: trade pays and soldiers are keen.
nations.constraint: Poor in coal and iron, and isolated by sanctions.

nations.name: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
nations.summary: Stalin’s union of republics from the Dniester to the Pacific, in its second five-year plan, newly in the League and allied with Czechoslovakia and Mongolia; Tannu Tuva is drawn with it.
nations.strength: Vast manpower and planned industry: armies are cheap to fill.
nations.constraint: Purges and immense distances: research and integration are slow.

nations.name: Republic of Poland
nations.summary: The restored republic between Germany and the Soviet Union, ruled by Piłsudski’s colonels since his death in 1935, with the port of Gdynia and the Free City of Danzig at the mouth of the Vistula.
nations.strength: A large army with a fighting tradition: soldiers fight well.
nations.constraint: Two great neighbours, and Ukrainian and Belarusian lands in the east that integrate slowly.

nations.name: Czechoslovak Republic
nations.summary: The democracy of Masaryk and, since December 1935, Beneš: industrial Bohemia behind its mountain forts, allied with France and the Soviet Union.
nations.strength: Škoda works and border forts: industry and fortification.
nations.constraint: Long borders and three million Germans in the Sudetenland.

nations.name: Federal State of Austria
nations.summary: The Alpine republic left in 1919, ruled by Schuschnigg’s Fatherland Front since Dollfuss’s murder and shielded by Italy against German annexation.
nations.strength: Alpine passes: forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Small, divided and coveted by Germany.

nations.name: Kingdom of Hungary
nations.summary: A kingdom without a king under the Regent Horthy, shorn of two-thirds of its land at Trianon and set on winning it back.
nations.strength: Revisionist fervour: soldiers fight hard.
nations.constraint: Small, ringed by the Little Entente and limited in arms.

nations.name: Kingdom of Romania
nations.summary: Greater Romania of 1918, with Transylvania, Bessarabia and Bukovina, the Ploiești oil fields, and alliances with Poland, the Little Entente and the Balkan Pact.
nations.strength: Oil and grain.
nations.constraint: Every neighbour claims a part of it: new lands integrate slowly.

nations.name: Kingdom of Yugoslavia
nations.summary: The kingdom of the South Slavs under the regent Prince Paul since King Alexander’s assassination in 1934, divided into nine banovinas.
nations.strength: Mountains and veterans: defenders fight well.
nations.constraint: Serbs and Croats at odds: land integrates slowly.

nations.name: Kingdom of Bulgaria
nations.summary: Tsar Boris’s kingdom, twice defeated and cut off from the Aegean, claiming Macedonia, Western Thrace and Southern Dobruja.
nations.strength: A hard army: soldiers fight well.
nations.constraint: Isolated and disarmed by the treaty of Neuilly.

nations.name: Kingdom of Greece
nations.summary: A kingdom again since November 1935 after a decade of republic and coups, with Thrace, Macedonia and the islands, and a merchant fleet on every sea.
nations.strength: Islands and ships.
nations.constraint: Political turmoil and a million refugees from Anatolia.

nations.name: Kingdom of Albania
nations.summary: King Zog’s mountain kingdom, bound to Italy by the treaties of Tirana and its loans.
nations.strength: Mountains: forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Poor and dependent on Italian money.

nations.name: Republic of Turkey
nations.summary: Atatürk’s republic of Anatolia and eastern Thrace, secular and modernising, and pressing to refortify the straits.
nations.strength: The straits and the hills of Anatolia: defenders fight well.
nations.constraint: Poor and rebuilding after a decade of war.

nations.name: Spanish Republic
nations.summary: The Second Republic, months before its civil war and divided between left and right, with the Moroccan protectorate, Ifni, Río de Oro and Spanish Guinea.
nations.strength: Mountains and a long border to defend: forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Little industry and a nation divided: provinces are restless.

nations.name: Portuguese Republic
nations.summary: Salazar’s Estado Novo, Britain’s oldest ally, ruling Angola, Mozambique, Guinea and Timor.
nations.strength: Atlantic trade.
nations.constraint: Small, poor and far from the rest of Europe.

nations.name: Kingdom of the Netherlands
nations.summary: A rich trading kingdom of ports and polders, neutral between Britain and Germany, and master of the East Indies and Surinam.
nations.strength: Commerce and the spice islands: trade and income above its size.
nations.constraint: Small and flat, between two great powers.

nations.name: Kingdom of Belgium
nations.summary: An industrial kingdom under Leopold III, allied with France, ruling the Congo and the mandate of Ruanda-Urundi; Luxembourg, in economic union with it, is drawn with it.
nations.strength: Coal and factories, and a guaranteed neutrality.
nations.constraint: On the road between France and Germany.

nations.name: Swiss Confederation
nations.summary: The armed neutral confederation of the Alpine cantons.
nations.strength: Mountain defence: militia and forts hold the passes.
nations.constraint: No coast and few resources.

nations.name: Kingdom of Denmark
nations.summary: A farming kingdom at the Baltic straits, with Greenland and the Faroes, and Iceland in personal union under its king.
nations.strength: Dairy and trade: income above its size.
nations.constraint: Small and next to Germany.

nations.name: Kingdom of Sweden
nations.summary: A long kingdom of forest, ore and timber, neutral and well armed.
nations.strength: Iron ore: industry starts cheaply.
nations.constraint: A long, thinly settled north.

nations.name: Kingdom of Norway
nations.summary: A seafaring kingdom of fjords whose merchant fleet sails every sea, neutral and lightly armed.
nations.strength: Shipping: trade pays more and straits cost less to cross.
nations.constraint: Mountains and few people.

nations.name: Republic of Finland
nations.summary: Independent since 1917, a republic of forests and lakes holding the Karelian Isthmus a day’s march from Leningrad.
nations.strength: Forests, lakes and ski troops: defenders fight well.
nations.constraint: Few people for a long border.

nations.name: Republic of Estonia
nations.summary: A small Baltic republic under Päts’s authoritarian rule, allied with Latvia.
nations.strength: Coast, marsh and forest: forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Very small, beside the Soviet Union.

nations.name: Republic of Latvia
nations.summary: Ulmanis’s republic at the mouth of the Daugava, trading through Riga and Liepāja.
nations.strength: Ports and timber: trade pays.
nations.constraint: Small, between Germany and the Soviet Union.

nations.name: Republic of Lithuania
nations.summary: Smetona’s republic, governed from Kaunas while its historic capital Vilnius is held by Poland, and master of Memel since 1923.
nations.strength: A people determined to keep its land.
nations.constraint: Small, claiming Vilnius and claimed for Memel.

nations.name: Kingdom of Egypt
nations.summary: A kingdom of the Nile, independent since 1922 but with British troops on the Suez Canal.
nations.strength: The Nile and its cotton: income above its size.
nations.constraint: British garrisons and a small army.

nations.name: Kingdom of Iraq
nations.summary: Independent since 1932 and bound to Britain by the treaty of 1930: a kingdom of the two rivers with the oil of Kirkuk.
nations.strength: Oil and the two rivers.
nations.constraint: A young state with restless tribes: land integrates slowly.

nations.name: Imperial State of Iran
nations.summary: Reza Shah’s modernising monarchy, renamed Iran in 1935; its north-west lies within this map.
nations.strength: Distance and mountains.
nations.constraint: Little industry: income and research are low.

nations.name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
nations.summary: The mountain kingdom of Zahir Shah, between the Soviet Union and British India.
nations.strength: Mountains and hardy tribes: soldiers fight well at home.
nations.constraint: Poor, remote and without industry.

nations.name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
nations.summary: Ibn Saud’s kingdom of Najd and the Hejaz, united in 1932, keeper of Mecca and Medina, with an American oil concession in Hasa.
nations.strength: Desert warriors: cavalry strikes hard.
nations.constraint: Sand and few people: no industry, little income.

nations.name: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen
nations.summary: The highland kingdom of Imam Yahya, independent since the Ottomans left in 1918 and at peace with Saudi Arabia since the treaty of Taif (1934).
nations.strength: Mountain strongholds: forts are cheap and defenders fight well.
nations.constraint: Isolated and poor.

nations.name: Sultanate of Muscat and Oman
nations.summary: A seafaring sultanate at the mouth of the Gulf, under British protection, at odds with the imamate of its interior.
nations.strength: Dhows and the Indian Ocean trade.
nations.constraint: Small, poor and divided.

nations.name: Kingdom of Nepal
nations.summary: A Himalayan kingdom ruled by the Rana prime ministers, closed to foreigners and a friend of British India.
nations.strength: Gurkha soldiers and mountain walls.
nations.constraint: Landlocked and poor.

nations.name: Republic of China
nations.summary: Chiang Kai-shek’s Nationalist China, governing from Nanking and fighting the Communists, with warlords in the provinces and Japan pressing on the north.
nations.strength: Numbers: an immense population and manpower.
nations.constraint: Warlords and foreign concessions: income, research and integration are weak.

nations.name: Empire of Manchukuo
nations.summary: The state Japan made of Manchuria and Jehol in 1932, under the last Qing emperor Puyi and the Kwantung Army.
nations.strength: Coal, iron and soybeans, and Japanese capital: supply flows.
nations.constraint: A puppet few recognise: land integrates slowly and others distrust it.

nations.name: Tibet
nations.summary: The Dalai Lama’s state on the roof of the world, independent in fact since 1913 and ruled by a regent since 1934.
nations.strength: The highest mountains on earth.
nations.constraint: Few people and no industry.

nations.name: Mongolian People’s Republic
nations.summary: The first Soviet satellite, on the steppe between the Soviet Union, China and Manchukuo, under the protection of the Red Army.
nations.strength: Horsemen of the steppe.
nations.constraint: Empty land: little income or industry.

nations.name: Empire of Japan
nations.summary: An island empire under rising military influence, master of Korea, Formosa and the South Seas mandate, with its creature Manchukuo on the continent; it has left the League and the naval treaties.
nations.strength: Discipline and a modern fleet: soldiers fight well and research is quick.
nations.constraint: Few raw materials at home.

nations.name: Kingdom of Siam
nations.summary: The only kingdom of South-East Asia to keep its independence, a constitutional monarchy since the revolution of 1932, between British Burma and French Indochina.
nations.strength: Diplomacy between the empires: others think well of it.
nations.constraint: Squeezed by two colonial powers.

nations.name: Ethiopian Empire
nations.summary: The ancient highland empire of Haile Selassie, invaded by Italy in October 1935 and fighting on in Tigray and the Ogaden.
nations.strength: Highland armies: defenders fight well at home.
nations.constraint: Little industry and no coast.

nations.name: Republic of Liberia
nations.summary: A small republic on the Grain Coast, independent since 1847 and dependent on Firestone’s rubber.
nations.strength: American friendship: others think well of it.
nations.constraint: Small, poor and indebted.

nations.name: Union of South Africa
nations.summary: The dominion of the Cape, Natal, the Transvaal and the Orange Free State, rich in gold, governing the mandate of South West Africa.
nations.strength: Gold and diamonds: income above its size.
nations.constraint: A divided white minority ruling a black majority.

nations.name: United States of America
nations.summary: The largest industrial economy in the world, still in the Depression under Roosevelt’s New Deal and neutral by law, with the Philippines, Hawaii, Alaska and the Panama Canal.
nations.strength: Industry and capital: income and research above everyone.
nations.constraint: A small standing army and a public set on neutrality.

nations.name: Dominion of Canada
nations.summary: A dominion free in its foreign policy since the Statute of Westminster (1931), from the Atlantic to the Pacific, its prairies hit by drought and depression.
nations.strength: Wheat, timber and rail: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: Few people for an immense land.

nations.name: United Mexican States
nations.summary: The republic of Cárdenas after the revolution: land reform, the oil fields of the Gulf and a quarrel with the foreign oil companies.
nations.strength: Silver and oil.
nations.constraint: Restless provinces after twenty years of revolution.

nations.name: Republic of Guatemala
nations.summary: The largest of the Central American republics, under the dictatorship of Ubico.
nations.strength: Coffee and highland forts.
nations.constraint: Small and poor.

nations.name: Republic of Honduras
nations.summary: A republic of banana coasts under Carías, where the fruit companies make and unmake governments.
nations.strength: Bananas: the fruit trade pays.
nations.constraint: Weak government.

nations.name: Republic of El Salvador
nations.summary: The smallest and most crowded Central American republic, under General Martínez since the massacre of 1932.
nations.strength: Coffee and a dense population.
nations.constraint: Very small.

nations.name: Republic of Nicaragua
nations.summary: A republic of lakes and volcanoes, left by the American marines in 1933 and dominated by Somoza’s National Guard.
nations.strength: The lakes and a canal route.
nations.constraint: A weak government.

nations.name: Republic of Costa Rica
nations.summary: A peaceful coffee republic with more teachers than soldiers.
nations.strength: Schools and stability: research and opinion are good.
nations.constraint: A tiny army.

nations.name: Republic of Panama
nations.summary: The isthmus republic beside the canal the United States runs.
nations.strength: The canal: trade pays and straits are cheap.
nations.constraint: Small and under American protection.

nations.name: Republic of Cuba
nations.summary: An island republic of sugar, under Batista’s influence since the revolution of 1933 and the eye of the United States.
nations.strength: Sugar: trade and income.
nations.constraint: An island under American tutelage.

nations.name: Republic of Haiti
nations.summary: The first black republic, left by the American marines in 1934.
nations.strength: Mountains and a fierce independence.
nations.constraint: Turmoil: the provinces are restless.

nations.name: Dominican Republic
nations.summary: The eastern republic of Hispaniola under Trujillo’s dictatorship.
nations.strength: Sugar and cacao.
nations.constraint: Debt and civil strife.

nations.name: Republic of Colombia
nations.summary: An Andean republic of coffee under the Liberals, which kept Leticia after its war with Peru in 1932–33.
nations.strength: Mountain valleys: forts are cheap.
nations.constraint: Divided by the Andes.

nations.name: United States of Venezuela
nations.summary: The oil republic of the Maracaibo basin, freed by Gómez’s death in December 1935 from twenty-seven years of his rule.
nations.strength: Oil beneath the lake.
nations.constraint: A dictatorship of one man.

nations.name: Republic of Ecuador
nations.summary: The republic on the equator, between the cacao coast and the volcanoes of the Andes, in dispute with Peru over the Amazon.
nations.strength: Cacao and the high valleys.
nations.constraint: Small and contested by Peru.

nations.name: Republic of Peru
nations.summary: The old viceroyalty of the Andes under Benavides, which regained Tacna in 1929 and gave up Leticia in 1934.
nations.strength: Guano, copper and the mountain wall.
nations.constraint: Defeat in the last war and a long frontier.

nations.name: United States of Brazil
nations.summary: The giant of South America under Vargas, a federal republic of coffee and rubber reaching deep into the Amazon.
nations.strength: Coffee and rubber: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: Vast and thinly settled: supply is slow.

nations.name: Republic of Bolivia
nations.summary: A landlocked republic of the high Andes, rich in tin, beaten by Paraguay in the Chaco War and still claiming the Chaco.
nations.strength: Tin and silver.
nations.constraint: Landlocked and thinly peopled.

nations.name: Republic of Paraguay
nations.summary: A small river republic, victorious in the Chaco War and holding most of the Chaco under the armistice of 1935.
nations.strength: A hard people.
nations.constraint: Depopulated and poor.

nations.name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
nations.summary: A small, prosperous republic of cattle and reforms on the River Plate, under Terra.
nations.strength: Beef and wool: income above its size.
nations.constraint: Small, between Argentina and Brazil.

nations.name: Argentine Republic
nations.summary: One of the richest countries in the world, exporting wheat and beef through Buenos Aires, ruled by the conservative Concordancia.
nations.strength: Grain and beef: trade and income.
nations.constraint: Its wealth depends on British markets and ships.

nations.name: Republic of Chile
nations.summary: The long republic of the Pacific coast, recovering from the collapse of nitrate, with a strong navy.
nations.strength: Nitrates and a Prussian-trained army.
nations.constraint: A long, thin country.

nations.name: Commonwealth of Australia
nations.summary: A federation of six states, its parliament in Canberra since 1927, governing Papua and the mandates of New Guinea and Nauru.
nations.strength: Wool and gold: trade pays well.
nations.constraint: An empty continent far from everyone.

nations.name: Dominion of New Zealand
nations.summary: The southernmost dominion, newly under its first Labour government, governing the mandate of Western Samoa.
nations.strength: Wool and butter.
nations.constraint: Small and remote.
